title: Tag-document linking
summary: define the optional one-way relationship from a canonical tag to an independently managed Analysis concept document
content_html:
Tag-document linking

Result

A canonical tag registry record may contain a doc_id identifying a document in the Analysis tags sub-scope. The field is optional, and the relationship does not give the tag exclusive ownership of the document: more than one tag may reference the same document.

The registry owns the one-way association. A document does not carry a tag_id back-reference, and documents that are not referenced by a tag remain valid. Either side may be deleted independently, so a document can become unreferenced and a registry link can become stale.

The document owns long-form contextual meaning. The registry description remains independent concise metadata: it may seed a newly created document once, but neither side synchronizes later edits to the other.

A linked registry record is:

{
  "tag_id": "moss",
  "group": "subject",
  "description": "<independent registry description>",
  "doc_id": "d-<immutable document ID>",
  "updated_at_utc": "<timestamp>"
}

An unlinked record omits doc_id.

Relationship contract

tag registry record
  -> optional doc_id
      -> one existing Analysis/tags document
      -> or stale after independent document deletion

other tag registry records
  -> may reference the same document
  • A registry record may omit doc_id.
  • When present, doc_id is an immutable Docs Viewer document identity intended to resolve within the configured Analysis tags sub-scope.
  • Multiple registry tags may reference the same document. The link is a reference, not an ownership or one-tag-to-one-document constraint.
  • Documents contain no tag_id field and may exist without a registry reference.
  • Deleting a tag leaves its document intact; the document may still be referenced by other tags.
  • Deleting a document does not update the tag registry. It may leave a stale doc_id.
  • tag_id is not editable through Edit Tag.
  • Neither document title nor content is used to infer or repair an association.

The checked-in registry currently has a nonblank, distinct doc_id on every row because of the completed bootstrap and the current New Tag workflow. That is the present dataset and workflow output, not the relationship cardinality.

Completed one-off bootstrap

The bootstrap took the 245 then-current flat registry rows, each without doc_id, allocated one new immutable ID per row, created 245 Analysis tags documents, and stored the IDs in tag_registry_v4.

Those allocated IDs were deliberately distinct so the migration could create new source files safely. The three pre-existing Analysis tags documents were left independent. Neither fact makes uniqueness between registry references an ongoing invariant.

Each generated document received the tag ID as its initial title, the registry description as one-time body content, and public visibility. The later Sub-Scope Report List Filter delivery seeded the registry group into document-owned group metadata once. Registry description/group and document content/group are independent after those seeds.

The sub-scope manifest remains the existing minimal public document-list contract. Public rows remain { doc_id, title }; canonical tag data is not projected into them.

Current creation and mutation behavior

  • New Tag creates a fresh Analysis tags document and the registry row in one transaction. The new row therefore receives a nonblank ID that is distinct from every existing document and registry ID.
  • The new document receives initial title, group, description content, and visibility from the creation request. Later registry and document edits do not synchronize.
  • Ordinary Edit Tag changes scalar group and description while preserving the existing doc_id. The modal does not expose, clear, replace, repair, or open the association.
  • Tag deletion removes the registry row and its existing alias/assignment effects. It does not delete the document.
  • Document deletion does not consult or update the registry.

The current New Tag planner also preflights the complete registry and rejects a missing, non-immutable, duplicate, or non-resolving existing doc_id. This is a stricter implementation boundary of the current create workflow. It must be relaxed before the UI can author the optional or shared-reference states allowed by the relationship contract; it does not make those states invalid registry relationships.

There is currently no focused association-inspection or repair workflow. Where a resolving link is consumed, its detail URL is derived rather than stored:

/docs/?scope=analysis&doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=<document ID>

Delivery Documents

  • Tag Document Bootstrap Delivery — one-off generation and association of the 245-row cutover set.
  • Sub-Scope Report List Filter Delivery — current document-group ownership, Concepts presentation, and first-class New Tag document creation.
  • Tag Link Management Delivery — first narrow New Tag to its own creation contract, then stop for review before discovering and freezing the links UI.

Association inspection, reassignment, clearing, shared-reference authoring, and stale-link repair are routed through that delivery without presupposing which controls or mutations the first UI slice needs.

Related Docs Viewer workflow

Dense sub-scope navigation and Markdown source editing belong to Manage Sub-Scope Documents, not this feature. That workflow was the management prerequisite for the completed bootstrap. Tag-document linking owns the optional registry association and derived public deep link; Docs Viewer owns the document lifecycle.

Collection-local selection, document controls, and adoption by applicable collection functions belong to Sub-Scope Index. The Analysis tags collection is a consumer and review surface for that generic Docs Viewer feature, not its owner.

Downstream semantic-token dependency

A future Tag semantic-token target can derive a stable destination from a resolving registry doc_id and the public subdoc route. An unlinked or stale association has no available document destination. Multiple tags may resolve to the same destination.

Tag semantic-token support remains separate follow-on work. It must not infer or repair a target from mutable document title, description, or content, and it must not add placeholder target-lookup rows without a usable href.

Durable Destinations

The optional registry link and navigation workflow belong in Tag Registry. The final source relationship belongs in Tag Source Data. Stable sub-scope list/detail behavior remains owned by Embedded Detail Documents.
